Hi Jordan / Priya — looping in Rishi (security) for any policy-level items. Quick technical answers and sample snippets below. Let me know if you want a short runbook or we can set up a call to walk the team through exports.

1) SOC 2 report: Operationally we maintain a current Type II; Marissa can share the PDF via our secure portal once an NDA is in place.

2) Immutability / WORM: For Hosted Redwood customers we provide a managed export function that can write logs to an S3/GCS bucket you control. If you use your managed bucket, you can enable S3 Object Lock (WORM) in your account — Redwood's export writes with server-side encryption but does not override your bucket-level WORM settings. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide an export pipeline with an optionally enforced WORM layer as part of the deployment.

3) Payload redaction: By default API logs capture request/response metadata and model inputs truncated to X bytes (configurable). PII-sensitive fields are not auto-identified by default. We offer a regex-based scrubber that can be enabled at the tenant level to redact common PII (emails, SSNs). We also support a webhook-based log sink so you can run custom redaction before storage.

4) Log formats & retention:
  - Admin logs: JSON entries with user, action, resource, timestamp, request_id. Example: {"time": "2026-06-19T07:11:22Z", "user": "marissa.co@redwood.ai", "action": "grant_role", "resource": "project-123", "request_id": "req-abc123"} 
  - API logs: model name, model_version, latency_ms, token_count, request_id; payloads included up to configurable byte limit.
  - Default retention: 90 days; configurable up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private contracts.

5) Exports: We support ad-hoc CSV/JSON exports from Console, scheduled exports to your bucket, and bulk exports via our API.

Attachments: I’ve attached a redacted sample log export (small sample) and a short tech-note.

Cheers,
